stem.text: The charge stored in a battery is modeled by a differentiable function B of time t, measured in minutes, whose rate of change is \( B'(t) = - \frac{65 e^{- \frac{t}{6}}}{6} \) watt-hours per minute, for \( 0 \le t \le 18 \). Using a calculator, find \( B'(5) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( B'(5) = -4.708 \), so at time t = 5 minutes the charge stored in the battery is decreasing at a rate of 4.708 watt-hours per minute.

worked_solution.text: With a calculator, \( B'(5) = -4.708 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at time t = 5 minutes the charge stored in the battery is decreasing at a rate of 4.708 watt-hours per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change

options.label: \( B'(5) = -4.708 \), so when the charge stored in the battery is 5 watt-hours it is decreasing at a rate of 4.708 watt-hours per minute.
options.derivation: the independent variable never named, so the input is read as a value of the quantity rather than a time

options.derivation: the rate of change of a non-motion quantity called a velocity
